clue.text: Did he regret violent interrogation?

indicators.note: violent suggests the letters of the first three words are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A questioner wonders whether a suspect felt remorse after a rough grilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' looks like part of the definition, but it is the anagram signal working on DIDHEREGRET; the definition is just 'interrogation'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for harsh, prolonged questioning of a suspect, often by police.

clue.text: Job centre supporting range for vagrant

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits underneath, so the Job centre goes below

parts.note: a range is a cooker, and a hob is its cooking top

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle letter of the word Job

explanation.surface: A Jobcentre helping out a tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jobcentre is a UK state employment office, which is the surface picture; here 'Job centre' is just the middle letter O, placed under HOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is an American word for a homeless wanderer or tramp.

clue.text: Split payment for lease

definitions.meaning: split as a noun means a tear or rip
the regular money paid to a landlord for a let property

explanation.definitionFit: A rent is a tear in fabric, and rent is also the regular sum a tenant pays the landlord.

clue.text: December, except the middle, should get a dry spell

indicators.note: except the middle keeps only the first and last letters of December

parts.note: should means ought, as in you should go

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster warns that December, apart from mid-month, will be rainless.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long period without rain.

clue.text: Cut at the bottom of fig tree

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its final letter, so take the last of fig

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Someone notices a wound low down on a fig tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a long deep wound or slash.

clue.text: The issue is execution for treason

indicators.note: execution here means beheading, so the word for treason loses its head letter

parts.note: sedition is incitement against the state, close to treason

explanation.surface: A historian notes that the penalty for treason was death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'execution' signals beheading: SEDITION loses its first letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a newspaper or magazine is one edition of it.

clue.text: Girl fronting a sporting occasion

indicators.note: fronting means coming in front, so the girl word stands before the a

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman leads the way at a sports event.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive sporting event, as in a swimming gala.

clue.text: Riddle in which head drinks with the queen

parts.note: head as in mind, the brain
teas are drinks
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A puzzle in which a monarch shares a cuppa with a headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword shorthand for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle or problem that taxes the mind, much like a riddle.

clue.text: One is crossed by distant blonde

indicators.note: is crossed by means the first piece has the second running across it, so it sits inside

parts.note: distant means far away
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone separated by distance from a fair-haired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair hair is light-coloured, i.e. blonde.

clue.text: One's sunk if one misses this last order!

definitions.text: One's sunk if one misses this last order!

parts.words: One's sunk if one misses this last order!
parts.note: read literally: a sailor who fails to obey the final command on a foundering vessel goes down with it

explanation.definitionFit: The order given when a vessel is going down, telling everyone to leave it.

clue.text: Party returned independence to holiday island

indicators.note: returned means the party word is read backwards

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
I is a standard abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: A political party came back granting freedom to a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Lab is the Labour Party, a major British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indonesian island famed as a tourist destination.

clue.text: Look mostly at a politician's elevated viewpoint?

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the look word

parts.note: observe means look at
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: Watching closely a Conservative MP's lofty perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the last E off OBSERVE; 'at' is a link. A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer's building, often on high ground, giving a view of the sky; the question mark flags the playful definition.

clue.text: A mess in the centre of the study?

parts.note: mid means in the middle
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Chaos in the middle of someone's study.
explanation.definitionFit: A midden is a dunghill or heap of refuse, hence a mess.

clue.text: Italian spirit with revolutionary French bread

parts.note: brio is the Italian word for vigour and verve
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: Combining Italian liveliness with a radical French loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a reversal signal, but it is Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a soft, rich French bun or loaf.

clue.text: Makes money from setting snare

indicators.note: setting means arranging, so the letters of snare are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A trapper profits from laying traps.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain money through work.

clue.text: Channel 5 is admitted to be financially sound

indicators.note: is admitted means the number is let inside the channel word

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A TV channel is given a licence to be in the black.
explanation.walkthrough: Channel 5 is a British TV station; here 'Channel' is the Solent, a sea strait off southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A solvent firm has enough assets to pay its debts.

clue.text: Continue to be detained by house guests

indicators.note: to be detained by means the answer is held within the words house guests

explanation.surface: A host is told to carry on while guests keep them occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: To segue is to move smoothly on from one thing to the next.

clue.text: Legal support for drug extract

indicators.note: in a down clue the support sits below, so the legal word goes under the drug letter

parts.note: E is short for the drug ecstasy
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: A lawyer backs the legalisation of narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out a response or information.

clue.text: Captured, thanks to Mr Livingstone

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
Ken Livingstone, former Mayor of London

explanation.surface: Someone seized, credited to the London politician.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thanks; Ken Livingstone was London's first elected mayor.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken means seized or caught.

clue.text: Concludes there's no time for cares

indicators.note: there's no means the time letter is removed from the caring word

parts.note: tends means cares for

explanation.surface: Someone finishes, having no time for looking after people.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to bring it to a close.

clue.text: God-fearing south American city

parts.note: pi is informal for pious

explanation.surface: A devout city in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south American' looks like one phrase but gives S and A separately; PI is crossword shorthand for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisa is an Italian city, famous for its leaning tower.

clue.text: Case of sedition exposed police informer

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: out means revealed or exposed

explanation.surface: A sedition case lays bare a grass in the police.
explanation.walkthrough: SNOUT is British slang for a police informer, a grass.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for someone who passes tips to the police.

clue.text: Hitler's revolutionary slide

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning things over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the name with its S

explanation.surface: The dictator's radical downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: To slither is to slide along sinuously.

clue.text: Wastes time giving guns to troop leader

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word troop

parts.note: rifles are guns

explanation.surface: Arming the head of a troop with firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle is to idle or fritter away time.

clue.text: Wreckers in museum starting to loot and strip

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: starting to takes the first letters of loot and strip

explanation.surface: Thieves in a museum begin looting and stripping exhibits.
explanation.walkthrough: The Victoria and Albert Museum in London is known as the V and A, written out here as VANDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vandals are people who wilfully destroy property.

clue.text: Before the young child became a recluse

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A little one grew up to live alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, someone living in seclusion.

clue.text: Dog brush

definitions.meaning: to dog is to follow closely
a fox's bushy ... is called its brush

explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to follow them, and a fox's brush is its tail.

clue.text: An urge to provide it with central heating

explanation.surface: A desire to install central heating.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless desire.

clue.text: A problem for baby to turn

definitions.meaning: trapped air in an infant's stomach

explanation.definitionFit: Babies suffer from trapped gas, and to wind is to twist or coil.

clue.text: It's nothing, just a little twitch of the ear

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
a tic is a small involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a slight twitch of the ear as nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective relating to the ear.

clue.text: Give up after hearing of top player

indicators.note: hearing of means the word for a top player is heard, not seen

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament

explanation.surface: Someone concedes after news of a leading tennis star.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or yield.

clue.text: Communication cord?

parts.note: not the emergency handle on a train but a linked series of messages passed from person to person

explanation.definitionFit: A message forwarded from one recipient to many others, forming a linked series.

clue.text: Run for the people

definitions.meaning: a run is a contest of speed

explanation.definitionFit: A race is a contest of speed, and also a group of people sharing descent.

clue.text: Detects rare exchange in confidential information

indicators.note: exchange means the letters of the first two words swap places

explanation.surface: A spy uncovers a rare swap of classified material.
explanation.definitionFit: A method or recipe kept private by a business.
